intro_html: The iconic "Swiss Pyramid" – a relentless 1700 m climb with extraordinary views of Lake Thun and the Bernese Alps. Popular funicular descent option.

routes.title_html: Mülenen → Niesen Kulm — the classic "Swiss Pyramid" ascent — A relentless but non-technical 1700 m climb from the valley floor, gaining elevation through pasture, forest, and alpine terrain. Iconic views of Lake Thun dominate the descent.

getting_there.by_pt_html: Train + PostBus: From Thun (main station), take the regional train toward Spiez (~10 min), then board PostBus line 1 or 2 toward Mülenen (~30 min from Spiez, final stop). Combined SBB + PostBus journey ≈60 min total. From Interlaken, take the scenic train to Thun (~20 min) then proceed as above. Swiss Travel Pass covers both; check current PostBus route numbers on sbb.ch.
getting_there.by_car_html: Via Simmental: From Thun, drive south toward Spiez, then follow the scenic Simmental valley road toward Mülenen (1680m elevation, ~40 km from Thun center, ~45–50 min). Excellent parking at the Mülenen trailhead near the valley station; ample space and facilities. Alternatively, approach from Bern via Spiez. Road access is open year-round but can be busy on weekends.

lapse_rate.valley_ref: Thun (428 m) — main valley reference for Thunersee region
lapse_rate.example_html: 20 °C at Thun → ~7 °C at Niesen Kulm (2362 m) — typical July afternoon. Wind exposure on the summit is high; bring extra layers.

weather.season_html: July–September is optimal: stable weather, minimal snow, warm(ish) days. June can see snow patches above 1800 m. October deteriorates with increasing cloud and wind. The Niesen-Bahn funicular operates May–October, so plan descent accordingly if using the railway.

items_html:
• Hiking poles

safety_html: Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
